title: Steamed Artichokes with Garlic Cream Dip
description: Microwave-steamed whole artichokes, leaf-by-leaf through a punchy garlic cream — the pile of spent leaves is part of the theater.
source: Developed with the chef, cooked 2026-09-07 (artichoke night)

changelog.note: First publish — microwave steam replaced the boil mid-cook and earned the primary spot: faster, one less pot, off the critical path.

steps.text: Trim the 2 artichokes: cut each stem flush so it sits upright, slice the top inch off, snip the thorn tips with scissors. Work fast and get them to the steam — cut artichoke grays in minutes.
steps.why: The graying is oxidation and purely cosmetic; lemon-rubbing prevents it, but speed works nearly as well and needs nothing.

steps.text: Start the dip: put the 4 smashed garlic cloves and ¾ cup heavy cream at the barest simmer for 12 minutes, until a clove mashes against the pan wall with no resistance. Mash them all into the cream, lid on, off heat.
steps.why: Steeping mellows the garlic from sharp to sweet — raw garlic in cream never loses its bite.

steps.text: Rinse the artichokes and leave them dripping wet. Set them upside down in a microwave-safe bowl with ½ cup water, a pinch of fine salt scattered into the wet leaves.
steps.why: Upside down puts the dense base in the hottest zone, and the clinging rinse water becomes steam inside the leaves.

steps.text: Cover tightly — a plate on top, or plastic wrap with one corner vented — and microwave on high 8 minutes. Knife-test the stem base: no grip means done. Not yet? Continue in 2-minute rounds; two big globes can take 12 to 14 total.
Leave covered 5 minutes after the microwave stops, then uncover away from your face.
steps.why: The covered rest lets carryover steam finish the centers evenly — and the trapped cloud when you uncover is genuinely dangerous to lean over.

steps.text: Drain the artichokes upside down in a colander 5 minutes.
steps.why: The leaves hold hot water like shingles, and every trapped spoonful thins your dip leaf by leaf.

steps.text: Finish the dip: return the garlic cream to medium-low and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon and a finger-swipe holds its track. Off heat, whisk in the 1 tbsp cold butter. Season LOUDER than the rest of the plate: fine salt confidently, plus a real grind of black pepper.
steps.why: A dip meets each bite for only a second, so it needs more seasoning than a sauce that coats — quiet dips disappear.

steps.text: Serve immediately: dip each leaf fat-end first and scrape between your teeth. When the leaves go thin and papery, spoon out the fuzzy choke — everything beneath it is the heart. Quarter it and drag it through what's left.

notes.title: No boiling pot, on purpose
notes.body: Microwave steaming takes the artichokes off the stovetop's critical path, cooks in a third of the time, and skips a pot. If you'd rather boil: 30–40 minutes in salted, lemony water, weighted down with a small lid so they stay submerged.

notes.title: Doneness is two tests
notes.body: An outer leaf pulls free with zero fight AND a knife slides into the stem base like butter. Use both — leaves can loosen before the heart is done.

plating: Upright on the flat-cut base, dip in a warm ramekin at sharing distance, flaky salt over the artichoke last. An empty bowl on the table for spent leaves — the growing pile is part of the fun.
elevations: ½ tsp Dijon whisked into the finished dip — tang the plate is otherwise missing.
A few drops of lemon juice in the dip if the house has one.
Grated Parmesan into the hot dip for a salty, nutty depth.
pairings: Crusty bread for the leftover dip
variations: Making the purée too? Steep once for both: 14 cloves in 2 cups cream, reserve ½ cup for the dip before the purée gets the rest.
